crash.when: 0.1.13 and 0.1.14 with the disk tier and image input both on: ~10 s into the first long prompt (the first run of 4096 positions handed to the store), or at the first switch of conversations (the leaving write)
crash.why: with a projector loaded every server_tokens has has_mtmd set, media in it or not; persist_runs compared the prompt with its runs through get_tokens(). It now reads get_text_tokens(), after checking that the prompt holds no media (it already did).
crash.who: a profile saved before 0.1.13 carries prompt_cache_disk true and vision true, both defaults then; the profile on this machine does

slot_check: apply_slot_state_guard compared a slot's tokens with its memory before a prompt batch only when has_mtmd was false, i.e. never with a projector loaded (the default profile). It now skips only prompts that hold media; no false alarm over a 137K prompt, the image stress test, or the switches below.

unified_memory_variable.finding: nothing reads GGML_HIP_ENABLE_UNIFIED_MEMORY: ggml reads GGML_CUDA_ENABLE_UNIFIED_MEMORY (getenv != nullptr, so any value turns it on) and the HIP runtime neither; checked in the source and, ASCII and UTF-16, in all 32 DLLs of the release plus System32's amdhip64*.dll
unified_memory_variable.consequence: the manager's reload "in shared memory" after an out-of-memory exit ran the same program again, and the +4.2% prefill credited to =0 (docs/results.md) was run-to-run variation; 0.1.15 sets neither variable and retires the profile field shared_vram

memory_during_a_137k_prompt.note: GiB of the server process; 0.1.10's runtime has 0.1.8's compute-buffer behaviour (the reallocation fixed in 0.1.11) and its disk tier on, as the issue #1 reporter ran it

0.1.10_runtime.log: prompt_save: disk cache: not enough memory to gather 4044.525 MiB of state (twice); an earlier run of the same probe failed the prompt at 57344 tokens with "decode() failed: bad allocation"

memory_during_a_137k_prompt.reading: the two ~3.3 GiB steps are the target compute buffer reallocated as the attention window grows; the freed one keeps its commit until the process exits. Here they stay in the carve; the reporter saw shared GPU memory climb to its 15.8 GB limit instead, where they also take system RAM.
